correctness.rationale: Strict log-determinant concavity and injectivity of grounded Laplacian edge parameters establish the unique unrestricted optimizer; price-invariant torus translations enforce two homogeneous positive edge classes. Fourier eigenvalues give the exact matrix-tree product. A strict Cauchy--Schwarz derivative proves uniqueness of the finite stationarity ratio. The root-of-unity Poisson-kernel identity gives a single-sum resolvent; a uniform analytic expansion and periodic trapezoidal quadrature give F_n(u/n^2)=nH(u)-1+O(n^-1), including its derivative. Monotone inversion gives the n^-2 term and positive n^-3 correction; the high-/low-price constants follow by dominated convergence. The extracted standard-library checker reproduces 124 finite exact and numerical tests; those tests are ancillary to proof.

originality.rationale: The exact lattice product of Tzeng--Wu is prior, not a novelty claim. The inspected primary results do not include optimization over independent conductances with separate direction costs or the singular Q=kappa*n optimum with an explicit n^-3 correction. Known square-torus resistance optimization has a different trace-inverse objective; D-optimal fixed-width prism optimization cannot imply the growing-two-dimensional integral coth law. A stronger unlocated optimization theorem would still be an originality risk.

value.rationale: Optimizing determinant-based network connectivity with two direction-specific edge prices on a two-dimensional periodic graph is a natural resource allocation problem. A fixed graph has an inverse-first-power large-price optimum but an infinite grid has an inverse-second-power law. The theorem identifies and proves the intervening Q=kappa*n crossover with an exact hyperbolic-cotangent integral and first finite-size correction, a structural outcome not captured by evaluating an already-known spanning-tree polynomial.
